records.name: PAWS (Philadelphia Animal Welfare Society)
records.summary: A Philadelphia animal rescue with an Old City adoption center and two spay and neuter clinics. Volunteers can help at the shelter, and people can foster animals while they wait for homes.
records.what_you_do: Help care for animals at the adoption center, and open your home to foster kittens or other animals until they are adopted.

schedule.text: Volunteer shifts and foster placements run through the year; check the volunteer page for current openings

locations.label: Grays Ferry Spay/Neuter and Wellness Clinic

cost.text: Volunteering and fostering are unpaid; the group asks for donations

first_step.how: Use the Become a Volunteer page or email the foster team to start a foster application
first_step.basis: The site has a plain volunteer page and a foster page that explain how to start

records.notes: Homepage lists a news item dated 10.06.26. Phone numbers are the adoption center number; the clinic numbers are 215-298-9680 (Grays Ferry) and 215-545-9600 (Northeast). Foster inquiries for kittens go to foster@phillypaws.org.

records.name: ACCT Philly
records.summary: The city's open intake animal shelter. Volunteers can walk dogs, help with adoptions, or drive animals to new homes, and people can foster animals to free up space.
records.what_you_do: Walk dogs, help at adoption events, transport animals, or take a foster animal home until it is adopted.

schedule.text: Volunteer orientations are held through the year; check the volunteer page for dates

first_step.how: Apply through Become a Volunteer and attend a volunteer orientation
first_step.basis: The site names volunteer orientations as the way in

records.notes: Shelter street address and phone were not on the homepage; visit the Hours and Directions page before going. A search summary also mentioned an ACCT trap-neuter-return program with an undated news story; not confirmed on the group's own site, so not written as a fact.

records.name: PURR (Philadelphia Urgent Rescue and Relief)
records.summary: An all-volunteer cat rescue run on donations. It trims colonies of outdoor cats, takes in sick or unwanted cats, runs a sanctuary, and places cats through adoption and foster homes.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer with cat rescue and trap-neuter-return work, foster a cat, or help at the cat cafe in Bridesburg.

schedule.text: Volunteer and foster sign-up is open; no regular meeting schedule published

locations.label: PURR Cat Cafe
locations.notes: Bridesburg neighborhood; no street address on the group's site

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer page or the foster application on the group's site
first_step.basis: The site has separate pages to volunteer, foster and request help, and it is open to new volunteers

records.notes: The site is current but its posts are undated, so status is probably_active rather than active. Mailing address appears in a directory listing only, not on the group's site, so it is left out.

records.name: Schuylkill Center Wildlife Clinic
records.summary: The wildlife clinic at the Schuylkill Center cares for sick, hurt and orphaned native wildlife. Volunteers help with animal care and clinic work after a training session.
records.what_you_do: Feed and clean enclosures, prepare food, and help with care of small mammals, birds, reptiles and amphibians.

schedule.text: Clinic support volunteers work two 4-hour shifts a month; animal care volunteers commit to a weekly 4-hour shift; training sessions are offered a few times a year

first_step.how: Register for a volunteer training session, then send in the volunteer waiver and application and finish the online ethics and safety courses
first_step.basis: Training, a waiver and online courses are required before any hands-on work

records.notes: Newest dated item is a volunteer training session in February 2025, which the page marks as passed, so status is probably_active, not active. Call the wildlife line (215-482-7300, option 2) to confirm the clinic is taking volunteers now. Wildlife hotline is option 2 on the same number. Clinic support volunteers must be 16 or older; animal care volunteers 18 or older.

records.name: Philadelphia Metro Wildlife Center
records.summary: A licensed wildlife rehabilitation center that takes in injured and orphaned wild animals from the Philadelphia region. Its volunteers do much of the daily feeding and cleaning.
records.what_you_do: Feed, wash and clean up after wild animals, and help with the center's education work such as its wildlife ambassador program.

schedule.text: Animal care runs every day, so volunteer shifts are set with staff

locations.label: Philadelphia Metro Wildlife Center
locations.notes: Norristown, just outside the city; serves the Philadelphia area

first_step.how: Call 267-416-9453 and ask about volunteering; injured wildlife must be discussed with staff by phone before bringing it in
first_step.basis: The center takes volunteers and is reachable by phone; the group's own page does not spell out a volunteer process

records.notes: Volunteer count (about 60) and volunteer tasks come from an earlier news profile, not the group's site. Its newest dated item on its site is a newsletter from January 2026. Not in Philadelphia city limits, so in_city is false. Its site does not list volunteer openings.

records.name: Philadelphia Zoo Volunteer Programs
records.summary: The Philadelphia Zoo runs several volunteer programs, from docent training to shifts at special events and internships in animal care and conservation education.
records.what_you_do: Train as a docent to lead visitor tours, help with special events, or join a seasonal internship in animal care or education.

schedule.text: Docent training is in modules from April to March; special events shifts are morning, afternoon or all day; internships run in fall, spring and summer terms

cost.text: Volunteering is unpaid; the zoo does not publish a fee

first_step.how: Submit the online application for the program you want, then do an interview, background check and training
first_step.basis: Every program needs an application, interview, background check and training before shifts start

records.notes: Minimum ages: docents 21, special events 13 for family shifts and 21 for adult-only events, Volun-TEENS 14 to 17. Docent training modules and internship windows are listed on the page for 2026 and 2027. Zoo street address was not on the pages I could read, so no locations are written.

records.name: Fletcher Street Urban Riding Club
records.summary: A nonprofit riding club in North Philadelphia that teaches young people to ride and care for horses, with life skills and school support built in. Riding is free for kids and families.
records.what_you_do: Learn to ride, groom and care for horses, and take part in club life that centers on school and goals.

schedule.text: Riding and stable work happen on a regular weekly schedule set by the club

cost.text: Riding is free for kids and families

first_step.how: Fill out the member request form on the group's site
first_step.basis: Open to the public through a member request form, and riding is free; the site does not state an age minimum

records.notes: Founded 2004 by Ellis Ferrell Jr. Newest dated news is a July 2025 CBS report; the group's own site has no dated posts. Address was not on the pages read; the club sits in North Philadelphia (Strawberry Mansion area per a search summary). Phone and email are on the contact page, which was not readable.

records.name: Work to Ride
records.summary: A free horsemanship program for under-resourced young people in Philadelphia, based at the Chamounix Equestrian Center in Fairmount Park. It runs a summer camp and one-day farm and horse programs for kids.
records.what_you_do: Kids learn horsemanship and equine sports; volunteers help with programs at the stables.

schedule.text: Summer camp for kids 7 to 13; other programs run on a schedule the group announces

cost.text: The group calls its riding free for under-resourced youth; camp scholarships are available

first_step.how: Email wtr@worktoride.net or call (215) 877-4419; volunteers sign up through the volunteer form (volunteers must be over 14)
first_step.basis: Public contact details and a volunteer form are listed; the group's page does not describe a join process for youth

records.notes: The homepage has a news entry dated October 6, 2026. The program operates from the Chamounix stables that a 2022 city listing describes at 98 Chamounix Drive; the group's own page gives no street address. Chamounix also runs lessons and polo for fee-paying riders, not written as a separate record.

records.name: Philadelphia Saddle Club at Monastery Stables
records.summary: A membership club at Monastery Stables in the Wissahickon Valley where members ride horses without owning one. Members share the chores of caring for the horses.
records.what_you_do: Ride the horses at set times each week, take part in shared barn chores, and ride the Wissahickon trails with other members.

schedule.text: Members book a horse for a set time each week and can ride as often as they like; the club has a waiting list

cost.text: Dues are not published on the group's site

first_step.how: Email monasterystables@gmail.com and ask about joining the waiting list
first_step.basis: Membership is needed, there is often a waiting list, and the site does not publish how to join

records.notes: The site mentions a Lantern Night on October 17 with no year and does not describe the club itself, so status is unknown. Membership count (14 or 15) and monthly fee come from older news and an organizer page, not the group's site; check with the club. Monastery Stables also runs a volunteer and Friends program; the group is a volunteer community of riders.

records.name: Courtesy Stable
records.summary: A riding stable offering lessons, leasing and trail riding in Wissahickon Valley Park. It runs as a riding business with no community program on its site.
records.notes: Riding lessons business. Excluded under the rule for businesses with no community program. Site copyright is 2024 but it is not dated evidence.

records.name: Northwestern Stables
records.summary: A riding stable offering lessons, boarding and summer day camps in Chestnut Hill and the Wissahickon area.
records.notes: Riding business with lessons and camps; excluded under the rule for businesses with no community program. Newest dated item is a Facebook post about a fall schooling show, with no year shown, so the date is approximate.

notes: Thin wave: the search results for this family were mostly older articles, and few groups had their own current pages. The biggest gaps are dog owner groups (no active nonprofit with its own site found), pet bird clubs (none found in Philadelphia), and cat TNR groups beyond PURR and ACCT. Schuylkill Center's clinic status was checked: its page lists a February 2025 training as the newest dated item and no closure was found, so it is probably_active with a call-to-confirm note. Pegasus Therapeutic Riding Academy is the most important unchecked lead because it serves people with disabilities. WebSearch budget: 9 of 10 used, 1 kept spare. Records written: 11 (9 publish, 2 not_a_group). Business stables were excluded under the businesses rule. Nothing in this file was modified outside the output path; no git used.
